title: Deployment-owned embedded Cyclotron for Papyrus publications
description:
PLANNING ONLY. Ryan requested filing and design before implementation. This issue is not authorization to build runtime features, deploy, change cloud permissions, publish packages, push, or migrate production data. Keep open pending design review and separate implementation authorization.

Purpose: a Papyrus deployment runs an embedded cyclotron with no separate Cyclotron lab and no external Cyclotron-owned store. All classifier data, labels, history, learning and prediction versions belong to that deployment and its own persistence lifecycle. Concrete acceptance example: DataParade with a limited posts section. Use the same real shared Cyclotron monitoring, steering and human-label/explanation components as remote mode; do not fork a reduced UI or invent a separate decision contract.

Milestones: deployment-owned persistence and execution, then DataParade end-to-end mode-parity acceptance. Consume the shared contract/components milestone owned once under the remote initiative; local deployment-owned persistence mechanics remain undecided. No implicit remote synchronization or mode migration is authorized.

Preserve optional curated-example priming (decision-flywheel-da886c09-7acb-45d3-acf8-c81585f26d8a), its preview/revision/explicit-label acceptance contract, and separate existing scholarly research-paper and web-summary transformations. Priming must never become an onboarding gate. Common input items are distinct from publication-specific decisions; one publication accepting an item must never implicitly label another output.

Open design questions (not decisions): stable item/revision, classifier/output and publication/deployment identities; binding configuration and changes; account/tenant permissions; service-role authentication without long-lived keys; per-output feedback and learning isolation; shared-item deduplication and provenance; versioned predictions and stale review handling; retry/idempotency, availability and recovery; remote/embedded mode parity. Choose no identity algorithm, auth provider, cloud topology or storage technology by filing these cards.

Planning completion: clear authority boundary and linked reusable contracts plus behavior stories. Future delivery completion requires authorized DataParade-style decide/review/steer/restart tests with no remote lab/storage dependency.
